title: Huawei's Non-Folding Wide-Screen Phone Is Coming in September With a 7,000mAh Battery
excerpt: Building on the Pura X's success, Huawei is preparing a candybar-style smartphone with a 16:10 display ratio and flagship specs — and it's arriving sooner than expected.
body:
• Huawei is finalizing a non-folding smartphone with a wide 16:10 display aspect ratio, similar to its Pura X foldable but without the hinge
  • The device will pack a 7,000mAh+ battery, a Kirin 9-series chipset, a 50MP main camera with 1/1.3-inch sensor, and a 50MP periscope telephoto
  • Originally scheduled for Q4, the phone has been moved up to a September launch after being finalized ahead of schedule
  • Oppo is working on a similar wide-screen phone with a 6.3-inch to 6.4-inch 16:10 display, expected in the first half of 2027

Huawei is preparing to launch a non-folding smartphone with a wide-screen display, bringing the tablet-like viewing experience of its Pura X foldable to a traditional candybar form factor. According to multiple leaks corroborated by GSMArena, the device is now expected to arrive in September — months earlier than the originally rumored October-to-December window.

The phone will feature a display with a 16:10 aspect ratio (some leaks say 16:9), a dramatic departure from the 20:9 ratio used by most current smartphones. The wider screen provides significantly more horizontal viewing area, reducing letterboxing during video playback and offering a more comfortable experience for web browsing, document editing, and split-screen multitasking.

Flagship Specs Without the Fold

Leaked specifications paint a picture of a full flagship device. According to tipster Digital Chat Station on Weibo, whose leak history has proven reliable, the phone will be powered by a Kirin 9-series chipset and pack a battery capacity of at least 7,000mAh — substantially larger than the Pura X foldable's 4,720mAh cell.

https://x.com/sondesix/status/2090386096459067504

The camera system includes a 50MP primary sensor using a large 1/1.3-inch sensor, a 50MP periscope telephoto camera, and a multispectral sensor. The device reportedly features a flat display panel with a borderless, zero-bezel visual appearance, and the engineering prototype is described as surprisingly thin and lightweight despite its larger footprint.

"By removing the complex folding mechanism, Huawei could offer this phone at a more competitive price point while improving durability and reducing weight."

— Gadget Pilipinas

Why Wide Screens Are Having a Moment

The wide-screen phone builds directly on the success of Huawei's Pura X, launched in March 2025 as the world's first wide-screen foldable. The Pura X's 6.3-inch inner display with its 16:10 ratio was praised for offering a mini-tablet experience that made competing flip phones feel cramped by comparison.

The wider aspect ratio has since gained significant industry traction. Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8, launched in July 2026, adopted a wide-screen design and accounted for 70% of the Z8 series pre-orders. Apple's first foldable iPhone is expected to feature a similar wide aspect ratio when it debuts later this fall. Xiaomi has also been spotted testing a wide-screen foldable.

A non-folding version eliminates the trade-offs that come with foldable engineering — the crease down the middle, the thickness when folded, and the significantly higher price tag — while preserving the viewing experience that made the form factor popular. Huawei apparently expects the device to sell well in China, based on the Pura X's market performance.

Competition Heating Up

Huawei is not alone in exploring non-folding wide screens. According to GSMArena, Oppo is also developing a phone with a 6.3-inch to 6.4-inch screen and a 16:10 aspect ratio, featuring a flagship chipset and a triple rear camera setup with periscope telephoto. That device is expected in the first half of 2027.

The trend represents a potential rethinking of smartphone ergonomics that has been locked into tall, narrow form factors for years. While a wider phone sacrifices one-handed usability, it gains real estate for content consumption, productivity, and gaming — use cases that increasingly define how people use their devices.

What's Next

Huawei has not officially confirmed the device or its name. The phone is expected to launch in China first, with no word yet on international availability. Pricing has not been leaked, but removing the foldable mechanism should place it significantly below the Pura X's CNY 7,499 ($1,037) starting price.

For the global smartphone market, the device could signal the beginning of a broader shift. If Huawei, Oppo, and eventually others bring wide-screen candybar phones to market alongside their foldable counterparts, the 20:9 aspect ratio that has dominated smartphone design for years may finally face a credible challenger.
nri_angle: Huawei's wide-screen non-foldable challenges conventional smartphone design globally, with the wider display trend being adopted by Samsung, Apple, and Oppo.
